differences: The paper says about 23% of the 75,000 trials were discarded (about 58,000 kept). The deposit's own manual good/bad label (param column 25) marks 3.4% of rows, and that is what excluded_by_authors holds. The rest of the 23% comes from further criteria of the authors' analysis code (blinks, saccades at the step, double saccades, saccades to the first ramp); the deposit's flag columns for those criteria are kept in trial_info, but no combination of them was fitted to the 23%, so the share is not reproduced here.

17 block files (850 trials) sit in the archive folder of one participant but carry the number of another participant inside (and in their file names): 7 blocks in folder 8 are labelled 13 and 10 blocks in folder 15 are labelled 16. Participants 8 and 15 would otherwise lack exactly those blocks and participants 13 and 16 would have those block labels twice, so the folder is taken as the true participant; this is inferred, not stated by the authors.
README of the deposit lists param column 25 as 'good or bad (0 or 1)'; the authors' extraction code stores good = 0, bad = 1, which is how it is read here.

Column 29 ('trigger time less than 50 ms' in the README) is computed as trigger time < 80 ms in the authors' code; it is kept as flag_trigger_time_short. The README of the deposit marks column 33 'not used'; it is kept as flag_col33_not_used.

Sessions are not labelled in the deposit. The block labels run 10 to 109; the condition (clear or blurred) is constant within each run of ten labels and alternates between runs, so session = (block label - 10) // 10 + 1 is inferred from that, and the order of blocks in time is assumed to follow the labels.
Rows with no saccade after the second target step (smooth trials) have empty saccade columns; the deposit stores zeros there.
